why.terrace: Boothen End, loud and known in England; no famous organised group.

why.conscience: Nothing notable found; community trust work (estimate).
why.ground: bet365 Stadium, 30,089-seat out-of-town bowl, not usually full.
why.rituals: Delilah adopted as anthem since the 1970s, well known in England.

why.women: Stoke City Women in the third tier (4th in 2025-26).

why.terrace: Loud Welsh support, known in the EFL; no famous organised group.
why.city: Capital's football club and Welsh identity, but the city shares itself with rugby.

why.conscience: FA fined the club £15,000 and imposed an action plan over homophobic chanting at Chelsea, Dec 2025.
why.ground: Cardiff City Stadium, 33,316, often far from full.
why.contender: Promoted from League One 2026; Premier League seasons 2013-14 and 2018-19.

why.women: Cardiff City Women: Welsh top tier, champions three seasons to 2025, runners-up 2025-26.

why.terrace: Loud Kop end at the Racecourse, widely seen through Welcome to Wrexham.
why.city: The club is the identity of the north Wales working town (city since 2022).
why.voice: Supporters' trust owned the club 2011-21; 98.6% of members approved the takeover; less power now.
why.conscience: Nothing notable found; UN Football for the Goals (2025), Gresford disaster remembrance on the kit.
why.ground: Racecourse Ground, 10,771, compact, historic (oldest international stadium in use), sold out.
why.contender: Three straight promotions; 7th in the Championship 2025-26.
why.rituals: Global fame comes from the documentary rather than matchday traditions.
why.stewardship: Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney; Allyn family ~15%, Apollo Sports Capital (private equity) minority stake since Dec 2025.
why.women: Wrexham AFC Women won the Welsh top tier (Adran Premier) 2025-26, 2,918 at the decider.
why.intensity: Estimate: Parkinson sides physical and direct, mixed.

why.terrace: Organised supporters' association, no famous singing end.
why.city: Bolton's one club in a working Lancashire town; ground is in Horwich.
why.voice: Supporters' association exists; no documented decision-making role.
why.conscience: Nothing notable found (crowd trouble v Wigan 2021, no sanction found); community programmes.

why.women: Estimate: women's side in the lower national divisions.
why.intensity: Estimate: Evatt/Schumacher sides possession-attacking in League One.
